reader_question: Which everyday answers rest on the most claims?
grade_line: Graded by the atlas, claim by claim: our count of its register of claims
title: Of the atlas’s 16 everyday answers, the one on voting and public influence rests on the most claims, 42.
measure_line: Claims in the atlas’s register behind each of its 16 everyday answers, 433 claims in all, as of the atlas’s snapshot of October 15, 2026, United States.
source_line: Source: Oath & Action’s systems atlas, Who Do They Answer To?, claims register, 433 claims across 16 everyday questions, snapshot of October 15, 2026, United States. The atlas checked 432 of the 433 claims on that date. Grades are the atlas’s own, defined on its evidence page; a claim’s grade covers that claim alone.
notes: The answer on roads, bridges and transit rests on the fewest, 13.
A count shows how many claims an answer cites.

The answer with the most claims takes the reader’s question “Which election decides who represents me, and how can I influence the people who decide?”; the one with the fewest, “Why is the repair on my street taking so long?”
alt: Lollipops rank the atlas’s 16 everyday answers by the claims behind each. Voting and public influence leads with 42, then pay and working conditions with 39 and housing costs with 34; roads, bridges and transit has the fewest, 13. The 16 answers rest on 433 claims in all.
chart_notes: The answer on voting and public influence, which the title names, ends in a red dot; the other 15 answers are gray.
